To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cumulative inflammatory potential of serum samples from CAD patients is significantly higher than healthy controls, as assessed by gene expression in primary endothelial cells.

the serum of patients with coronary artery diseases induces endothelial cell activation and that this activation can be measured using a biosensor assay that is not dependent on the measurement of specific serum inflammatory biomarkers.
serum from coronary artery disease patients induces greater endothelial expression of adhesion molecules (ICAM- and VCAM-1) and cytokines (IL-8) than serum from healthy subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel serum inflammatory potential in patients with CAD, which may be an indicator of disease activity and progression.
the characterization of a novel endothelium-based biosensor assay that can potentially serve as a biomarker for vascular inflammation.
the identification and quantification of inflammatory potential in the serum of patients with CAD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serum inflammatory potential of patients with CAD, as assessed by the endothelial cell assay, is significantly higher than in healthy subjects.
the cumulative endothelial biosensor is more sensitive to the presence of CAD than any individual inflammatory biomarker.
endothelial cells are a cumulative biosensor that is activated in patients with coronary artery diseases and this activation is not dependent on serum inflammatory biomarker levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cumulative inflammatory potential in serum from patients with stable coronary artery disease is increased compared to healthy control subjects, as assessed by a novel endothelial cell biosensor assay.
the endothelium is a useful biosensor for the detection of systemic inflammatory factors in CAD patients, which are not necessarily reflected in the circulating cytokine levels.
the cumulative inflammatory potential of serum, as measured by endothelial cell gene expression, may be a more useful biomarker than the individual components of the inflammatory process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
serum from CAD patients has an enhanced inflammatory potential that can be measured by endothelial cell gene expression.
the endothelial cell biosensor assay is an attractive tool to assess the net inflammatory potential in CAD patients.
the endothelial biosensor may serve as a useful tool in the future for assessing the cumulative inflammatory potential of the serum.
